decisions.reason: Acacia nilotica at 45 cm is a confirmed non-native species obstructing the footprint. Statutory compensation is 14-37 saplings, identical to what a native of the same girth would require — but the recommended mix is native-weighted, so the replanting is not simply more Subabul.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is age-equivalent and SPECIES-BLIND. The statutory count is identical for a native and a non-native tree. This tool applies the same count to both and expresses the native/non-native distinction in the recommended species mix instead, which is the ecologically meaningful lever and stays inside the Act.

relocation.method_note: Composite = 0.35*spacing + 0.25*connectivity + 0.25*flood + 0.15*access. Each criterion is reported separately so it can be challenged on its own. Flood uses distance to NATURAL watercourses (nallas, rivers) as exposure; engineered stormwater proximity is deliberately not a siting bonus.
relocation.data_limit: Only PMC-mapped parks and gardens are considered. Private gardens, institutional grounds and undeveloped municipal plots are not in this dataset, so viable_count understates the true options.
